title: Navigating Tricks
intro: The shortest section in the book, and possibly the highest value per word. Getting the playhead and the view where you want them, instantly, is the difference between working and fiddling.

tips.t: Z is the only zoom command you need
tips.d: Select anything and press Z to zoom that selection to fill the window. Press Z again to return to where you were. With nothing selected it fits the whole project.
Hold ⌃⌥ and drag a box around any part of the arrangement to zoom straight to it. Hold ⌃⌥ and click empty space to zoom back out.

tips.t: Navigate by marker with the number keys
tips.d: Markers 1 through 9 are jumpable directly. Set your song sections as markers and the whole arrangement is one keypress away.

It plays the selected region from its start and stops at its end without touching the locators or the position you were working at. Search the command name in Key Commands and give it a key — it is not on one by default.

tips.t: Jump to an exact bar with the Go to Position dialog
tips.d: Press / and type a bar number. Faster and more accurate than dragging the playhead, especially in a long project.
Two‑finger swipe left and right on a trackpad, or hold ⇧ while scrolling with a wheel mouse. Keep your hand off the scrollbar entirely.

tips.t: Use the Cycle area as a bookmark
tips.d: Set the locators around the part you are working on with U. Even when you play elsewhere, clicking the cycle bar in the ruler takes you straight back to it.

tips.t: Toggle Catch to stop the screen running away
tips.d: The Catch button makes the view follow the playhead. Click it off when you are doing detailed editing and the view will hold still while the song plays. Search “Catch Playhead Position” in Key Commands to put it on a key.
